headline: Google's earnings miss sends GOOG down nearly 12% last night, while PLS.AX tumbles 8% today on ongoing lithium weakness — but the long-term thesis on both remains intact.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: A shocker of a night for Google. Alphabet missed profit expectations last night, with ad revenue growth slowing and heavy AI spending weighing on results. Investors sold off hard — the stock dropped nearly 12%. The long-term AI story at Google isn't dead (they just launched Gemini 4 Carbon), but the market wanted better numbers and didn't get them.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS fell 8% today — a rough session with no company-specific news attached, which suggests this is broader lithium market weakness dragging it down. Lithium prices remain depressed globally as supply continues to outpace EV demand growth. PLS is now down nearly 60% from your entry price.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF slipped 1.2% today, largely dragged lower by Google's overnight earnings miss — several big AI-linked stocks in the index felt the ripple effect. The broader AI thematic is still strong (Google just released a new frontier model), so this looks like short-term noise.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets gave back a little today, down about 1%. No single big catalyst — general risk-off sentiment globally as US markets softened overnight and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East simmered.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG had a quiet positive day, up 0.3%, helped by the ASX 200 climbing 0.5%. The diversified nature of this fund means Google's overnight pain was cushioned by other holdings doing fine.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft actually reported strong earnings last night — $92.3 billion in quarterly revenue, with cloud and AI products performing well. The slight share price dip of about 1% looks like profit-taking after a big run, not a signal about the business. Results were solid.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two was essentially flat last night, up just 0.06%. No earnings news — the stock is coasting ahead of the GTA 6 launch. Bank of America this week recommended buying the stock ahead of the release, citing long-term upside.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was nearly unchanged today, down just 0.08%. It tracks the entire US share market, so last night's mild S&P 500 dip (−0.31%) barely moved the needle here.

movers.name: DHHF ETF
movers.note: Essentially flat today — DHHF barely moved, down just 0.02%. Nothing to see here; this broadly diversified fund is doing exactly what it's supposed to do: absorb daily noise without drama.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Earnings miss — hold, don't panic
watch_today.detail: Google fell nearly 12% last night after Alphabet missed profit expectations. Ad revenue slowed and AI infrastructure spending was high. It stings, but the long-term story — Google's dominant search position, YouTube, cloud, and now Gemini 4 Carbon — hasn't changed. For a long-term holder, this is painful but not a reason to sell. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Down 8% today — still a long-term hold
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had another ugly day, falling 8%, and is now down nearly 60% from your entry. There's no company-specific news — this is the lithium market staying depressed. If you believe in the EV battery demand story over the next 5–10 years, the thesis isn't broken, just severely delayed. Don't sell into weakness unless your conviction in the long-term story has changed.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Strong earnings — hold with confidence
watch_today.detail: Microsoft posted $92.3 billion in quarterly revenue last night, beating expectations. Azure cloud and AI products are clearly paying off. The modest -1% dip looks like profit-taking, not a sign of trouble. This is one of your best performers (up ~18.7% overall) and the business is firing. Nothing to do here.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 launch window approaching — hold
watch_today.detail: Take-Two was flat last night but Bank of America has come out this week recommending buying ahead of the GTA 6 launch, citing long-term gains. The game's map is reportedly nearly the size of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined. You're still down ~9.5% overall — patience is the play here as the launch gets closer.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike likely Tuesday (Melbourne Cup Day)
watch_today.detail: Markets are now pricing in a fifth RBA interest rate hike on Cup Day next Tuesday. CommBank economists and Market Index are both forecasting it, with a sixth hike now a 50-50 chance. Higher rates put pressure on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on how your ETFs react heading into next week.

watch_today.title: Middle East tension: Iran war risk rising post-midterms
watch_today.detail: The US has warned Gulf allies to prepare for a possible resumption of strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections. Vice President Vance has reportedly made outreach to Tehran, but Iran says current mediation proposals are unacceptable. Oil is already at $100/barrel — any escalation could spike energy costs globally and rattle markets.

world.summary: The big global stories today: a potential Iran war restart looming after US midterms, Brazil's political drama as Flávio Bolsonaro flees to the US, a US judge shutting down an attempt to set aside 20,000 California ballots, and India's Jio Platforms crashing into the global top 5 telcos.

stories.title: US warns allies: Iran strikes could resume after midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has quietly warned Gulf allies to prepare for a 'short, intense' resumption of military action against Iran after next week's midterm elections. Vice President Vance has made direct outreach to Tehran, but Iran says the latest mediation proposals are completely unacceptable. Oil is already sitting at around $100 a barrel — if strikes resume, expect energy prices to spike, which flows through to petrol prices and inflation for everyday Australians. This is one to watch very closely next week.

stories.title: Brazil: Flávio Bolsonaro flees to the US after election loss
stories.why_it_matters: Flávio Bolsonaro — son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro — has reportedly fled to the United States following an election loss in Brazil. The Bolsonaro family's political future in Brazil looks increasingly troubled, with the country's courts pursuing various legal actions against the family. Brazil is a major emerging market, and political instability there is worth watching if you hold emerging market ETFs like VGE.

stories.title: US judge blocks attempt to segregate 20,000 California ballots
stories.source: The New York Times / ABC News
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has rejected a Trump administration request to set aside around 20,000 California ballots, calling it 'attempted election interference.' The judge ruled the move had no legal basis. With US midterm elections happening next week, this is a significant moment — it signals courts are willing to push back hard on attempts to challenge ballot counts before results are even in. US political stability matters for global markets.

stories.title: Jio Platforms breaks into global top 5 telcos after ASX-style listing
stories.why_it_matters: India's Jio Platforms — owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries — has broken into the global top 5 telecom companies by market cap after its stock market listing. It's a sign of how fast India's tech and digital economy is growing. For those holding emerging market ETFs like VGE, India is now one of the largest weightings — this kind of milestone reflects that the India story is very much alive.

stories.title: Obama rallies for Georgia Senator Ossoff, laughs off Trump attacks
stories.why_it_matters: Barack Obama has hit the campaign trail in Georgia, rallying for incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff ahead of next week's US midterm elections. Obama used a rally speech to laugh off recent attacks from Trump, saying the response was outsized for what he called a joke. With control of the US Senate potentially on the line, this race matters — a change in Senate control would affect US fiscal and regulatory policy, with flow-on effects for global markets.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a solid day, up 0.5% to close near 8,892. Meanwhile, last night on Wall Street the picture was messier — the NASDAQ dropped 1.3% as Google's earnings miss spooked tech investors. The S&P 500 fell a more modest 0.3%. Oil is sitting at $100.87 a barrel, slightly down but still historically elevated. Gold eased off a touch. The Aussie dollar is basically flat at around 70.3 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session on the ASX today, up half a percent, broadly helped by strength in resources and financials.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's S&P 500 eased slightly, down 0.3%, as Google's profit miss weighed on sentiment without derailing the broader market.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The tech-heavy NASDAQ took a harder hit last night, down 1.3%, dragged by Alphabet's disappointing earnings result.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil slipped about 1.9% last night but remains above $100 — still near multi-year highs, keeping fuel costs elevated. Geopolitical Iran risk could push it higher.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold dipped slightly, down 0.35%. At over $4,000 an ounce, it remains near record highs — a sign investors still want protection against uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was essentially unchanged, sitting just above 70 US cents. A stable currency means no big currency headwinds or tailwinds for your US holdings today.

politics.summary: Domestically it's all about interest rates, data centre regulation, and cost-of-living pressure. The RBA looks almost certain to hike rates again on Melbourne Cup Day next Tuesday, and Treasurer Chalmers is under fire for his handling of the inflation story.

stories.title: RBA almost certain to hike rates on Cup Day — fifth rise in a row
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia is now widely expected to raise interest rates for the fifth time at its November meeting next Tuesday — Melbourne Cup Day. CommBank economists have formally forecast the hike, and markets are now pricing it in at near-certainty. A sixth hike is now considered a 50-50 bet. Higher rates mean bigger mortgage repayments for millions of Australians and continued pressure on household budgets. Growth stocks also tend to struggle when rates rise.

stories.title: Labor to ban AI data centres from suburban areas, power cut threat for rule-breakers
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is moving to ban AI data centres from being built in suburban residential areas, and is threatening to cut power to any existing data centre that breaks the rules. This is a significant regulatory move — data centres are enormously energy-hungry and have been popping up in unexpected locations as demand for AI computing power explodes. It's a real tension: Australia wants to be part of the AI boom, but not at the cost of suburban liveability and power grid stability.

stories.title: Overseas student crackdown projected to cost universities $2 billion
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government's crackdown on international student numbers is now projected to cost Australian universities around $2 billion in lost revenue. Universities have heavily relied on full-fee-paying international students to cross-subsidise research and local student teaching. The cuts are designed to reduce pressure on housing and immigration, but they're hitting the education sector hard — with potential job losses and course cuts on the horizon.

stories.title: Chalmers under fire from economists over 'spin' on inflation
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is being called out by economists for what they're calling 'spin' around the latest inflation data. After a higher-than-expected inflation result, Chalmers has reportedly tried to downplay its significance and has lowered expectations for delivering promised fuel price relief. Independent economists say the numbers speak for themselves — inflation is still too high, the RBA will have to keep hiking, and government spending isn't helping. Chalmers is under increasing political pressure.

stories.title: Albanese's Digital Duty of Care Bill passes the House
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government's Digital Duty of Care Bill has passed the House of Representatives. The legislation targets serious online harms — and notably would ban AI chatbots from forming 'emotional intimacy' relationships with users. Tech companies operating in Australia will be required to meet new care obligations or face penalties. It's one of the more ambitious online safety laws passed anywhere in the world, and it puts Australia ahead of most other countries in regulating AI-human relationships.

ai.summary: Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon model is the big AI story of the week — it's beating rivals from OpenAI and Anthropic on most benchmarks. But Google's CEO may have used the launch to signal major workforce changes. Meanwhile, AI regulation is a growing global conversation.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon — beats GPT-6 and Claude on most benchmarks
stories.why_it_matters: Google has officially launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest and most powerful AI model. It outperforms OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 on most industry benchmarks — and does it at a fraction of the cost. The model is particularly noted for its ability to find and fix software security flaws automatically. The catch: you can't try it yet. Google is holding it back from public release while it scales up. For GOOG holders, this is a reminder the company is still at the frontier of AI despite last night's earnings miss.

stories.title: Sundar Pichai's Gemini launch may signal major job cuts at AI competitors
stories.why_it_matters: Alongside the Gemini 4 Carbon launch, Google CEO Sundar Pichai reportedly dropped hints that could signal significant job cuts — possibly at rival AI companies or even within Google itself. The timing, right as Alphabet's earnings disappointed, has analysts reading between the lines. The AI arms race is intensifying, and companies are under pressure to show that their massive AI spending is translating into real profits.

stories.title: ARK Invest ranks Google, Anthropic and OpenAI as top AI intelligence leaders
stories.why_it_matters: Investment firm ARK Invest has released its AI intelligence index, ranking Google, Anthropic and OpenAI as the three leading AI companies globally. This kind of ranking matters because ARK's assessments tend to drive investment flows — being named a top-3 AI player keeps Google in the conversation for institutional investors, even as the stock wobbled after earnings.

stories.title: Bloomberg: AI industry may regret backing Trump after midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Bloomberg is reporting that major US tech companies — including AI firms like Google, Microsoft and OpenAI — that have cosied up to the Trump administration may face a reckoning after next week's midterm elections if Democrats make gains. AI regulation and antitrust enforcement have become political footballs, and a shift in congressional power could mean more scrutiny for big tech. Worth watching as results come in next week.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done — Roosters beat the Knights 19-18 in an absolute nail-biter. Now the league's off-season is in full swing with the Walker saga, Rugby League World Cup semi-final scenarios heating up, and the AFL 2027 fixture dropping today.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters have won the 2026 NRL Grand Final, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in a one-point thriller at Accor Stadium. It doesn't get closer than that. The Roosters now head into the off-season as premiers, while the Knights will be left wondering what might have been after coming within a single point of the title.

stories.title: The Adam Walker saga: where will he end up? Ennis, Braith weigh in
stories.why_it_matters: The Adam Walker free agency saga is dominating NRL off-season talk. Fox Sports analysts Braith Anasta and Joel Encnis are weighing in — Braith reveals Walker 'doesn't want to go' to the Roosters despite being linked there, while Ennis shares his 'gut feeling' on where Walker will end up. There's also a surprise Bunnies (South Sydney) twist in the mix. The Roosters are reportedly in the market for a replacement halves partner regardless.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: semi-final scenarios for every team
stories.why_it_matters: The Rugby League World Cup 2026 is heading into the sharp end, with semi-final qualification scenarios now being mapped out for every competing nation. Fiji (the Bati) are among the contenders, and former Gold Coast Titan Jamayne Isaako is reportedly primed for a big performance after returning home for a parade in Fiji ahead of the knockout stages. Worth following as Australia and other nations chase the title.

stories.title: AFL 2027 fixture drops — Sydney wins big, St Kilda frozen out of primetime
stories.why_it_matters: The official AFL 2027 fixture has been released today, and there are clear winners and losers. The Sydney Swans have landed a prime draw with multiple high-profile timeslots, while St Kilda has been almost completely frozen out of primetime games. Fox Sports has graded every club's fixture — contenders got the marquee slots, while battlers are stuck in mid-afternoon obscurity. Pre-season momentum and TV exposure matter for clubs rebuilding.
